responsibility: Implements GCC’s target backend for the Renesas RX family, covering the ABI, data layout, register set, calling convention, target options, instruction selection, and final assembly details needed to turn generic RTL into RX machine code. The module’s core target-definition headers and hook implementation files (`rx.h`, `rx.c`/`rx.cc`, `rx-protos.h`, `rx-opts.h`) define RX-specific target macros, option-controlled behavior, address legality and legalization including small-data and PID modes, builtin expansion, cost and register handling, prologue/epilogue generation, and operand/assembly printing. Its machine-description files (`rx.md`, `predicates.md`, `constraints.md`, `rx-modes.def`) provide the RTL predicates, operand constraints, condition-code modes, instruction patterns, and scheduling data that drive RX instruction matching, expansion, branching, stack-multiple operations, and emission. The option and OS/format support files (`rx.opt`, `elf.opt`, `linux.h` and their documentation companions) supply RX command-line controls and ELF/Linux specializations such as assembler syntax, specs, predefined macros, and interrupt-related configuration, making this module the architecture-specific code-generation layer that distinguishes the RX port from neighboring GCC backends.
